source.dataset: Form EIA-861M, Sales and Revenue by State (residential)

title: Home electricity prices by state

unit.label: Residential price, cents per kWh (12-month average)

description: Average price households pay for electricity in each state, in cents per kilowatt-hour, over the latest 12 months.
howToRead: Each point averages the latest 12 months, weighted by how much electricity was sold, so summer and winter rate swings even out.
Price is total residential revenue divided by kilowatt-hours sold, so it includes fixed customer charges spread across usage.
caveats: The most recent months are preliminary and are revised when EIA publishes final annual data.
A higher price per kWh does not always mean a higher bill: homes in mild or efficient states may use far less power.
